summary: This Wikipedia article defines an ice age as a long period of reduced surface and atmospheric temperature with extensive ice sheets and alpine glaciers, and explains that Earth alternates between ice ages and greenhouse periods. It traces the history of ice age research from 18th- and 19th-century observations of erratic boulders to the theory's acceptance in the 1870s. It also covers the evidence for ice ages, the major ice ages in Earth's history, glacial and interglacial cycles, feedback processes, and proposed causes. The note is truncated before its sections on effects, future ice ages, and references.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of ice ages: their definition, history of research, geological evidence, major past ice ages, and causes.
key_facts: An ice age is defined as a long period of reduction in the temperature of Earth's surface and atmosphere, resulting in the presence or expansion of continental and polar ice sheets and alpine glaciers.
In glaciology, the term ice age is defined by the presence of extensive ice sheets in the northern and southern hemispheres, so the current Holocene period is an interglacial period of an ice age.
In 1742 Pierre Martel visited the valley of Chamonix in the Alps of Savoy and reported that inhabitants attributed erratic boulders to glaciers that had once extended much farther.
In a paper published in 1824, Jens Esmark proposed changes in climate as the cause of a sequence of worldwide ice ages, and attempted to show they originated from changes in Earth's orbit.
At the beginning of 1837, Karl Friedrich Schimper coined the term 'ice age' ('Eiszeit') for the period of the glaciers.
In July 1837 Louis Agassiz presented the ice age synthesis before the annual meeting of the Swiss Society for Natural Research at Neuchâtel, where the audience was very critical.
Louis Agassiz published his book Study on Glaciers ('Études sur les glaciers') in 1840 and omitted any mention of Schimper in it because of personal quarrels.
The ice age theory was fully accepted internationally in the second half of the 1870s, following the work of James Croll, including his 1875 book Climate and Time, in Their Geological Relations.
There have been at least five major ice ages in Earth's history: the Huronian, Cryogenian, Andean-Saharan, late Paleozoic, and the latest Quaternary Ice Age.
The Huronian ice age has been dated to around 2.4 to 2.1 billion years ago and was caused by the elimination of atmospheric methane during the Great Oxygenation Event.
The Cryogenian ice age occurred from 720 to 630 million years ago and may have produced a Snowball Earth in which glacial ice sheets reached the equator.
The Andean-Saharan ice age occurred from 460 to 420 million years ago, during the Late Ordovician and the Silurian period.
The Quaternary Glaciation started about 2.58 million years ago, and the last glacial period ended about 11,700 years ago.
The Himalayas are still rising by about 5 mm per year because the Indo-Australian plate is still moving at 67 mm/year.
According to a Nature Geoscience study, human emissions of carbon dioxide will defer the next glacial period, which otherwise would usually begin within 1,500 years.

entities.name: Pierre Martel
entities.role: Engineer and geographer living in Geneva who visited the valley of Chamonix in 1742 and published an account of his journey two years later

entities.name: Jean-Pierre Perraudin
entities.role: Carpenter and chamois hunter who explained erratic boulders in the Val de Bagnes as due to earlier glacier extension

entities.name: Jean de Charpentier
entities.role: Swiss-German geologist who initially rejected Perraudin's glacier theory and later became converted to it

entities.name: Daniel Tilas
entities.role: Swedish mining expert who in 1742 was the first to suggest drifting sea ice caused erratic boulders

entities.name: James Hutton
entities.role: Scottish philosopher and gentleman naturalist who in 1795 explained Alpine erratic boulders by glacier action

entities.name: Göran Wahlenberg
entities.role: Swedish botanist who in 1818 published his theory of a glaciation of the Scandinavian peninsula as a regional phenomenon

entities.name: Jens Esmark
entities.role: Danish-Norwegian geologist who argued in 1824 for a sequence of worldwide ice ages caused by changes in Earth's orbit

entities.name: Robert Jameson
entities.role: Professor at the University of Edinburgh who seemed relatively open to Esmark's ideas

entities.name: Albrecht Reinhard Bernhardi
entities.role: Geologist and professor of forestry who adopted Esmark's theory and in 1832 speculated about polar ice caps reaching the temperate zones

entities.name: Ignatz Venetz
entities.role: Engineer who concluded that Perraudin was right and that only ice could have caused the observed features

entities.name: Karl Friedrich Schimper
entities.role: German botanist who concluded ice transported the boulders and coined the term 'ice age'

entities.name: Louis Agassiz
entities.role: Scientist who developed with Schimper the theory of a sequence of glaciations and published Study on Glaciers in 1840

entities.name: James Croll
entities.role: Researcher whose work in the 1870s led to international acceptance of the ice age theory and a credible explanation of its causes

entities.name: Maureen Raymo
entities.role: Researcher who with William Ruddiman proposed that the Tibetan and Colorado Plateaus act as CO2 scrubbers

entities.name: William Ruddiman
entities.role: Researcher who with Maureen Raymo proposed the plateau CO2 scrubbing hypothesis

entities.name: Matthias Kuhle
entities.role: Scientist whose geological theory of ice age development relies on an ice sheet covering the Tibetan Plateau

entities.name: Ewing and Donn
entities.role: Researchers who in 1956 hypothesized that an ice-free Arctic Ocean leads to increased high-latitude snowfall

entities.name: Climate and Time, in Their Geological Relations
entities.role: 1875 book by James Croll that provided a credible explanation for the causes of ice ages

entities.name: Study on Glaciers ('Études sur les glaciers')
entities.role: 1840 book by Louis Agassiz presenting his glaciation theory

entities.name: Chamonix valley
entities.role: Alpine valley in Savoy visited by Pierre Martel in 1742, where inhabitants attributed erratic boulders to former glaciers

entities.name: Val de Bagnes
entities.role: Swiss Alpine valley where Perraudin explained erratic boulders and striations by former glacier cover

entities.name: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora
entities.role: Eruption that created an ice dam forming a proglacial lake above the Val de Bagnes

entities.name: Great Oxygenation Event
entities.role: Event during which the elimination of atmospheric methane was said to have caused the Huronian ice age

entities.name: Quaternary Glaciation
entities.role: Current ice age, which started about 2.58 million years ago and in which Earth is currently located

entities.name: Snowball Earth
entities.role: Hypothesized state during the Cryogenian period in which glacial ice sheets reached the equator
